title: Generational KV slab allocator and adaptive preemptive evictor with compaction-feedback
author: Maya Singh
description:
Context and motivation: production workloads showed long-tail memory amplification from small long-lived KV entries combined with transient hot entries. Existing single-slab allocators cause fragmentation and cascading spill events under bursty workloads. This PR introduces a generational slab allocator plus an adaptive preemptive evictor that cooperates with the scheduler and compaction feedback loop to reduce tail latency and decrease spill-to-disk rates.

What this PR does (high level): adds a 2-generation slab allocator (young/hot + old/stable), a lightweight predictive preemptive evictor that uses short-term access heat and sequence-length-aware heuristics to preemptively compact and spill low-utility objects, and an idle-time compactor that coalesces small free segments when the node is below CPU load threshold. Integrates eviction signals with the request scheduler so that large batching decisions can trigger opportunistic compaction outside of SLO windows.

Design details: generational slab keeps small fixed-size regions for young objects that are expected to be reaccessed; objects surviving an age threshold are promoted to the old slab where larger contiguous segments are favored to reduce fragmentation. The preemptive evictor maintains a lightweight priority queue keyed by exponentially-weighted recency/frequency and predicted remaining lifetime (based on access pattern and model-agnostic heuristics). When memory pressure approaches a high watermark the evictor will compact within the old slab first and then select preemptive candidates from young->old cross-boundary candidates to avoid leaving behind fragmented pockets. Compaction-feedback loop: compaction run statistics (reclaimed bytes per work unit, CPU cost, spill reduction) are fed to an adaptive cost model that tunes compaction aggressiveness and the promotion age threshold at runtime.

Compatibility and migration: allocator exposes a backward-compatible config knob (kv.generational.enabled) defaulting to off for rolling release; when enabled, a cooperative draining protocol migrates in-memory objects in small batches to avoid pause spikes. Private customers can toggle the preemptive policy independently (kv.evictor.mode = passive|adaptive|preemptive).

Benchmarks (summary): microbench with mixed read/write 80/20, 128B median item, bursty tail: peak resident set reduced by ~22%, observed spill-to-disk events reduced 3.7x, 95p latency improved by ~18% on p3.2xlarge profiled nodes. Production canary on a small Dedicated cluster reduced emergency spill incidents from 5/week to 1/week over a 48h window. See bench/kv_memory_bench.toml and attached plots in the internal artifact link.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for slab promotion/demotion and compaction boundaries - [x] Integration test for cooperative draining during rolling upgrade - [x] Bench harness and regression tests - [x] Feature flag and runtime tuning knobs - [x] Documentation: design doc and ops runbook

Notes: this PR focuses on allocator/evictor logic; it intentionally leaves deeper ML-based lifetime predictors for follow-ups (ENG-2034). The compactor runs are gated by a CPU threshold to avoid contention with kernel-bound batching during high-throughput windows.

Related: ENG-1892 (kv memory fragmentation), ENG-2034 (predictive TTL follow-up), infra/ops ticket for Dedicated canary scheduling.

review_comments: Evan Cho: Can you clarify how promotions avoid copy amplification under large-value workloads? Suggest measuring copy bytes in bench.
Maya Singh: Response: promotions are size-class aware; values > 16KB are kept out of young slab by default and use a direct allocation path. Added copy-bytes metric to bench and a note in docs.
Lena Hoffman: Request change: prefer configurable promotion age via runtime flag, and ensure compaction is throttled below N% CPU. Also add e2e canary steps.
Maya Singh: Response: added kv.promote_age_ms and compactor.cpu_threshold_pct config, updated ops runbook and canary checklist.
Marcus Li: Approve after CI passes and minor nits fixed (log level + comment).
merge_outcome: Merged after CI green and 2 approvals. Squash merge with test artifacts attached to the merge commit.
release_notes:
- Add generational slab allocator for KV cache to reduce fragmentation and tail spill events.
- Add adaptive preemptive evictor that uses short-term heat to preemptively compact and spill low-utility items.
- Idle-time compactor with runtime tuning to coalesce free segments.
Operators: enable via kv.generational.enabled; tune kv.promote_age_ms and kv.compactor.cpu_threshold_pct for your workload.
notes_for_ops: Rolling deploy: enable feature flag in staging and run the cooperative draining job (ops/kv/drain.sh) during low-traffic windows. Monitor kv.reclaimed_bytes, kv.spill_events, and system cpu utilization. Canary instructions in docs/kv-generational-design.md.
